body:
Stateless request/response is the right transport for this crate (see #62 for why a connection-oriented transport cannot amortize under process-per-request). What we are not doing is using the caching that stateless HTTP already gives us. This is the work that actually reduces cost and TTFT, and it is small.

## Good news first: our prefix is already stable

Checked against the source. `coding_system_prompt` (src/agent/config.rs:35-62) is a pure function of cwd, reasoning note, shell flag, and tool budget. No timestamps, no run ids, no randomness. Tool specs come from `tool_specs(allow_shell)` (src/tools.rs:492) in fixed order. So across rounds within a turn, and across turns of a session, the leading bytes are stable and cache-eligible. We are probably getting implicit cache hits already and cannot see them, because usage is discarded at src/adapter.rs:56 (#17).

That stability is currently an accident of good habits rather than a stated invariant, and nothing protects it. Any future change that puts a timestamp, a session id, a remaining-budget counter, or a reordered tool list into the prefix would silently drop the hit ratio to zero with no signal.

## Work

1. **Make prefix stability an invariant with a test.** Assert that two consecutive rounds of the same turn produce byte-identical leading segments up to the appended content, and that the tool list serializes in a fixed order. This is the guard that keeps the property once it is deliberate rather than lucky.

2. **Anthropic: place a `cache_control` breakpoint** at the end of the stable head (tools, system, and once #78 lands, the epoch summary). Four breakpoints available. Default TTL is 5 minutes and refreshes on every hit, so an active session stays warm at no extra cost.

3. **OpenAI: set `prompt_cache_key`** per session. Cached prefixes live on individual machines and routing depends on a hash of the leading tokens plus this key; without it, concurrent traffic sharing a prefix can overflow to a machine with no entry and take avoidable misses. This matters directly for our own workload, where several instances run concurrently against one key.

4. **Report the numbers** (already added to #17): cached versus uncached input tokens per call and a per-run hit ratio, from `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` / `cache_read_input_tokens`.

## Ordering

Item 4 first, because without measurement the other three are unfalsifiable. Item 1 next, since it protects a property we already have. Items 2 and 3 after, and both should be settings-driven per #63 rather than hardcoded per provider.

Related: #78 makes the epoch head the natural breakpoint location once checkpoint lines exist; this issue is the pre-kernel version and does not depend on it.
title: model_api: use prompt caching properly on stateless HTTP (breakpoints, cache key, prefix-stability invariant)
